methods.name: _agents
methods.summary: The agents a chat can be started with, by name.

methods.name: _add_agent
methods.summary: Add an agent of one of the three types: `remote` (an address it is reached at), `container` (an image each chat gets a container of) or `program` (a command run on this machine). A token, when a remote agent has one, is kept in this machine's keychain; its picture, when it has one, in the app's database.

params.name: kind
params.description: Its type; fixed once it is added. Absent: `remote`.

params.name: name
params.description: What the agent is called. Blank is refused with a message.

params.name: url
params.description: `remote`: the agent's address, a `ws` or `wss` URL where it speaks the Agent Client Protocol over a WebSocket (`acpd`'s `/acp`). Required for that type; left out for the others.

params.name: token
params.description: `remote`: a bearer token the agent's address wants, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` when the app connects. Blank or absent: none.

params.name: folder
params.description: The folder the agent's sessions work in: an absolute path. `remote`: on the agent's machine (blank: `/`). `container`: in the container, where each chat's own volume is mounted (blank: `/workspace`). `program`: a folder of this machine that is there, which the program starts in (required).

params.name: avatar
params.description: Its picture: a `data:image/png;base64,`, `data:image/jpeg;base64,` or `data:image/webp;base64,` URL (no SVG), as the page makes it from a chosen file. Blank or absent: none, and the page shows its initials.

params.name: command
params.description: `program` and `container`: the agent's command, the program then its arguments (`["claude-code-acp"]`), which speaks the Agent Client Protocol on its standard input and output. A program is looked up in this machine's `PATH`; a container's runs in the container. Required for those types; left out for `remote`.

params.name: image
params.description: `container`: the image each chat's container is made from, by name and tag (`agent-sysadmin:1`). It is built or pulled in the Containers app; this app only uses it. Required for that type.

params.name: skills_dir
params.description: `container`: the folder its skills are copied into, in the container, each skill a folder of its own named after it. An absolute path. Blank or absent: `/root/.claude/skills`.

params.name: skills
params.description: `container`: the names of the skills of the Skills app (`_skills`) it uses, copied into each new chat's container. Absent: none.

params.name: env
params.description: `program` and `container`: the environment variables its program is started with, each with its value written out or taken from a keychain item. Absent: none.

params.name: mcp
params.description: The MCP servers its sessions are given, besides this machine's own tools. Absent: none.

errors.message: The name is blank, what its type needs is missing or not one (a remote's ws or wss URL, a program's or a container's command, a container's image, a folder that is not an absolute path or, for a program, not a folder of this machine), a variable or an MCP server is not one (a name that cannot be one, two of the same name, a value and a keychain item both, a keychain item without its service or account, a stdio server without a command, an HTTP server without an http or https URL), a skill's name cannot be a folder's, the picture is not a PNG, JPEG or WebP data: URL or is too big, or the keychain did not take the token.

methods.name: _update_agent
methods.summary: Change an agent; its type stays. A chat's next connection reaches it as it is now. A container chat keeps the container it has: a change of the image, the command, the folders, the environment or the skills reaches the chats started after it.

params.name: agent
params.description: The id of one of `agents`.

params.name: name
params.description: What the agent is called. Blank is refused with a message.

params.name: url
params.description: `remote`: the agent's address, a `ws` or `wss` URL. Required for that type.

params.name: token
params.description: `remote`: a new bearer token. Absent: the token stays as it is.

params.name: forget
params.description: `remote`: forget the token the agent has.

params.name: folder
params.description: The folder the agent's sessions work in: an absolute path. `remote`: on the agent's machine (blank: `/`). `container`: in the container, where each chat's own volume is mounted (blank: `/workspace`). `program`: a folder of this machine that is there, which the program starts in (required).

params.name: avatar
params.description: A new picture, as `_add_agent` takes it. Absent: the picture stays as it is.

params.name: remove_avatar
params.description: Remove the picture the agent has.

params.name: command
params.description: `program` and `container`: the agent's command, the program then its arguments (`["claude-code-acp"]`), which speaks the Agent Client Protocol on its standard input and output. A program is looked up in this machine's `PATH`; a container's runs in the container. Required for those types; left out for `remote`.

params.name: image
params.description: `container`: the image each chat's container is made from, by name and tag (`agent-sysadmin:1`). It is built or pulled in the Containers app; this app only uses it. Required for that type.

params.name: skills_dir
params.description: `container`: the folder its skills are copied into, in the container, each skill a folder of its own named after it. An absolute path. Blank or absent: `/root/.claude/skills`.

params.name: skills
params.description: `container`: the names of the skills of the Skills app (`_skills`) it uses, copied into each new chat's container. In place of the ones it has. Absent: none.

params.name: env
params.description: `program` and `container`: the environment variables its program is started with, each with its value written out or taken from a keychain item. In place of the ones it has. Absent: none.

params.name: mcp
params.description: The MCP servers its sessions are given, besides this machine's own tools. In place of the ones it has. Absent: none.

errors.message: There is no such agent, or what is given is refused as `_add_agent` refuses it, or the keychain refused.

methods.name: _remove_agent
methods.summary: Remove an agent; a turn it is taking ends. A remote agent's token goes with it. The chats of a remote or a program agent stay, and can be read; a container agent's chats go with it, with their containers and volumes (its image stays: it is the Containers app's).

params.name: agent
params.description: The id of one of `agents`.

errors.message: There is no such agent, or Docker did not remove a container or a volume of its chats (Docker cannot be reached, say). What was removed before that stays removed.

methods.name: _engine
methods.summary: Whether Docker can be reached. A Docker that cannot be reached is an answer (`reachable` is false and says why), not an error.

methods.name: _connect
methods.summary: Choose the Docker container agents' chats run in, and answer whether it can be reached. The containers of the Docker chosen before are not touched: a chat whose container is not in the new one gets a new container on its next turn.

params.name: host
params.description: Where Docker listens: `unix:///path/docker.sock`, `tcp://host:2375` or `http://host:2375`. Empty for this machine's own Docker.

errors.message: The address is not one Docker can be reached at.

methods.name: _secrets
methods.summary: The items of the keychain the Keychain app keeps, by service and account, for a variable or a header to take its value from. No password is given: it is read when a program or a container is started, or a session is given its MCP servers.

errors.message: The Keychain app is not there (not installed, or not running), or it did not list its items.

methods.name: _skills
methods.summary: The skills of the Skills app a container agent can use, by name. When the Skills app is not there or does not answer, the list is empty and `problem` says why: it is an answer, not an error.

methods.name: _images
methods.summary: The images Docker has, by name and tag, for a container agent's image to be chosen from. When Docker cannot be reached the list is empty and `problem` says why: it is an answer, not an error.

methods.name: _chats
methods.summary: Every chat, the most recently used first.

methods.name: _open
methods.summary: A chat and everything said and done in it so far.

methods.name: _send
methods.summary: Say something in a chat, or start one with an agent by saying the first thing in it (`agent` instead of `chat`): a chat is only made when something is said. Answers at once with the chat as it now stands; what the agent says and does follows as `item` and `piece` events and ends with a `turn` event. A container chat's first turn makes its container, and a program chat's turn starts its program when it is not running.

params.name: chat
params.description: The chat to say it in. Without it, `agent` starts a new chat.

params.name: agent
params.description: The id of one of `agents`, to start a new chat with: used only without `chat`.

params.name: text
params.description: What to say. Blank is refused with a message.

errors.message: There is no such chat or agent, the message is blank, the agent is still answering, or the agent was removed.

methods.name: _answer
methods.summary: Answer a permission the agent asked for during its turn with one of the options it offered; its turn goes on.

params.name: item
params.description: The id of the `permission` item.

params.name: option
params.description: The `option_id` of one of the options in the item's data.

errors.message: There is no such chat or question, it is answered already, its turn is over, or the agent did not offer that option.

methods.name: _stop
methods.summary: Stop the agent's answer in a chat: the agent is asked to stop (its open questions are cancelled), and its turn ends when it has. What it said so far stays.

methods.name: _remove_chat
methods.summary: Delete a chat and everything in it: a container chat's container and volume too, and a program chat's program ends.

errors.message: There is no such chat, or Docker did not remove the chat's container or volume (Docker cannot be reached, say): the chat stays, and can be deleted again.

methods.name: _item
methods.summary: An item of a chat is new or changed during a turn: the whole item.

methods.name: _piece
methods.summary: Text is added to an item of a chat while it comes.

params.name: item
params.description: The id of the item.

params.name: text
params.description: The text added.

methods.name: _turn
methods.summary: The agent's turn in a chat is over, however it ended (complete, stopped or failed): read the chat again.

Kind.description: How a chat reaches the agent. `remote`: over a WebSocket, at its address. `container`: each chat runs the agent in a container of its own, made from an image, and speaks to it on the container's standard streams. `program`: each chat runs the agent's command on this machine, and speaks to it on the program's standard streams.

version.description: Docker's version, empty when it cannot be reached.

host.description: Where Docker is looked for, as given to `_connect`. Empty for this machine's own Docker.

problem.description: Why Docker cannot be reached, as a sentence. Empty when it can.

Secret.description: An item of the keychain the Keychain app keeps: what its password is for and whose it is there.

Variable.description: A name and its value: an environment variable, or a header sent to an MCP server. The value is written out (`value`) or is the password of a keychain item (`secret`), read when it is needed and never kept by the app.

name.description: An environment variable's name: letters, digits and `_`, not starting with a digit. A header's: no spaces and no `:`.

value.description: The value, written out. Absent with `secret`; absent without it is empty.

secret.description: The keychain item whose password is the value.

Server.description: An MCP server an agent's sessions are given. `stdio`: a program the agent starts where it runs (on its machine, in the container, or on this machine). `http`: a server at a URL, given only to an agent that takes MCP servers over HTTP.

command.description: `stdio`: the program, where the agent runs.

url.description: `http`: its address, an `http` or `https` URL. In a container, this machine is `host.docker.internal`.
`remote`: its address, a `ws` or `wss` URL. Empty for the other types.

token.description: `remote`: whether a bearer token is kept for it. The token itself never leaves the keychain.

folder.description: The folder its sessions work in: on its machine, in the container, or on this machine.

avatar.description: Its picture, a PNG, JPEG or WebP `data:` URL; empty when it has none.

command.description: `program` and `container`: the agent's command, the program then its arguments. Empty for `remote`.

image.description: `container`: the image its chats' containers are made from. Empty for the other types.

skills_dir.description: `container`: the folder its skills are copied into, in the container. Empty for the other types.

skills.description: `container`: the names of the Skills app's skills it uses.

env.description: `program` and `container`: the environment variables its program is started with. A keychain item is named, never its password.

mcp.description: The MCP servers its sessions are given.

SkillSummary.description: A skill of the Skills app: what it is called, which is the name of its folder, and what it is for.

problem.description: Why the Skills app gave no skills, as a sentence. Empty when it answered.

images.description: Each image by name and tag (`debian:stable`), in name order.

problem.description: Why Docker gave no images, as a sentence. Empty when it answered.

title.description: The first thing said in it, shortened; `New chat` until then.

agent.description: The name of the agent it is with.

agent_id.description: The id of the agent it is with (one of `agents`, unless that agent was removed).

updated.description: When it was last used, ISO 8601 in UTC.

Item.description: One thing said or done in a chat, in the order it happened.

kind.description: `user`: what the person said. `assistant`: what the agent said. `reasoning`: what it thought. `tool`: a tool call of its. `plan`: its plan for the turn. `permission`: a permission it asked for. `note`: something the person should know about the chat (the agent started a new session, it stopped short). `error`: a turn that failed.

text.description: `user`, `assistant`, `reasoning`, `note`, `error`: the text (`assistant` with a `name`: what the piece is, a link's name). `permission`: what the agent asks to do.

name.description: `tool`: the call's title. `assistant`: empty for text, else the kind of piece in `data`: `image`, `link` or `resource`.

data.description: JSON text, or empty. `assistant` with a `name`: the piece, `{ type: "image", mime_type, data }` (base64), `{ type: "link", uri, name }` or `{ type: "resource", uri, text }`. `tool`: `{ kind?, status?, content?, locations?, input?, output? }`: status `pending`, `in_progress`, `completed` or `failed`; content a list of pieces, `{ type: "text", text }`, an image, a link, a resource, `{ type: "diff", path, patch, new_file }` (`patch` a unified diff) or `{ type: "terminal", terminal_id }`; locations `{ path, line? }`; input and output JSON text. `plan`: `{ entries: [{ content, priority, status }] }` (priority `high`, `medium` or `low`; status `pending`, `in_progress` or `completed`). `permission`: `{ kind?, options: [{ option_id, name, kind }], chosen? }` with option kind `allow_once`, `allow_always`, `reject_once` or `reject_always`, and `chosen` the option the person picked.

done.description: False while it is still coming or still running; for a `permission`, while it waits for its answer.

waiting.description: The agent asked for a permission that has no answer yet.
